```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(plotly)
```

## About this presentation

**Date created: November 13, 2026**

This slide deck was built with R Markdown (`ioslides_presentation`) and the
`plotly` package.

- Plots are fully interactive: hover for details, zoom, pan, and click legend items
- Data: the built-in `mtcars` dataset (1974 Motor Trend road tests)
- Question: how do engine power and weight relate to fuel economy?

## Fuel economy vs. weight

```{r plot1}
mtcars$cyl_f <- factor(mtcars$cyl)
mtcars$car <- rownames(mtcars)

plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, color = ~cyl_f,
        colors = c("#2a9d8f", "#e9c46a", "#e63946"),
        type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        size = ~hp, sizes = c(10, 40),
        marker = list(opacity = 0.75, line = list(width = 1, color = "white")),
        text = ~paste0("<b>", car, "</b><br>", hp, " hp"),
        hoverinfo = "text+x+y",
        height = 430) %>%
  layout(title = "Heavier cars use more fuel (bubble size = horsepower)",
         xaxis = list(title = "Weight (1000 lbs)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Miles per gallon"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "Cylinders")))
```

## Efficiency by cylinder count

```{r plot2}
plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~cyl_f, y = ~mpg, color = ~cyl_f,
        colors = c("#2a9d8f", "#e9c46a", "#e63946"),
        type = "box", boxpoints = "all", jitter = 0.4, pointpos = 0,
        height = 430) %>%
  layout(title = "Fewer cylinders, better mileage",
         xaxis = list(title = "Cylinders"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Miles per gallon"),
         showlegend = FALSE)
```

## Three variables at once (rotate me!)

```{r plot3}
plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~hp, z = ~mpg, color = ~cyl_f,
        colors = c("#2a9d8f", "#e9c46a", "#e63946"),
        type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(size = 5),
        text = ~car, hoverinfo = "text",
        height = 430) %>%
  layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "Weight"),
                      yaxis = list(title = "Horsepower"),
                      zaxis = list(title = "MPG")))
```

## Conclusions

- Weight and horsepower both go with lower fuel economy
- Four-cylinder cars are the most efficient on average
- Interactive plots make it easy to explore individual cars
